trap-negation-contrast.evidence: Full read of the SU(2) example. Recomputed: v v-dagger / ||v||^2 is a rank-1 Hermitian projector of trace 1, so subtracting id_V/2 gives a traceless matrix; with v = e_1 the image is diag(1/2, -1/2), and under the standard identification su(2) = R^3 by (n . Pauli)/2 -> n the image sphere is indeed the unit S^2, so 'unit 2-sphere' checks out. The Schur argument at the end is correct: a G-fixed point of the adjoint representation commutes with all of SU(2), hence is scalar, hence zero once traceless. 'but the only traceless scalar is zero' is substantive mathematical contrast, not a trap; no other construction present.
trap-negation-contrast.notes: MATH FLAG (not a trap): the block mixes the Hermitian and anti-Hermitian conventions for su(2) by a factor of i. sigma([l]) = v v-dagger/||v||^2 - id_V/2 is traceless HERMITIAN, while the orbit representative named two lines later, (1/2) diag(i, -i), is traceless ANTI-Hermitian (genuinely in su(2)). Both readings are common, but not in one paragraph. PROPOSED: either state the identification used ('we identify su(2) with the traceless Hermitian matrices via X -> iX') or write the orbit representative as (1/2) diag(1, -1).
